name: @epic-web/workshop-mcp

tools.name: login
tools.description:
Start device authorization and store credentials after the user verifies.

Inputs:
- `workshopDirectory` (string, required) - Absolute path to the workshop root. Passing a /playground path is allowed and normalized. Examples: /Users/alice/workshops/react-fundamentals.

Returns: { verificationUrl, userCode, expiresInSeconds }

Examples:
- "Start login for a workshop" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react" }

Next steps:
- Ask the user to open the verification URL and enter the code.
- Call `get_user_info` to confirm authentication.

workshopDirectory.description: Absolute or relative path to the workshop root directory. Relative paths are resolved from the current working directory. Passing a /playground path is allowed and will be normalized to the workshop root.

tools.name: logout
tools.description:
Log the user out of the workshop host and clear cached credentials.

Inputs:
- `workshopDirectory` (string, required) - Absolute path to the workshop root. Examples: /Users/alice/workshops/react-fundamentals.

Returns: { loggedOut: true }

Examples:
- "Logout from the current workshop" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react" }

Next steps:
- Call `login` if the user wants to re-authenticate.

tools.name: set_playground
tools.description:
Set the playground to a specific exercise step or the next incomplete step.

Inputs:
- `workshopDirectory` (string, required) - Absolute path to the workshop root. Examples: /Users/alice/workshops/react-fundamentals.
- `exerciseNumber` (number, optional) - Exercise number to open. Omit to continue to the next incomplete step. Examples: 1, 5.
- `stepNumber` (number, optional) - Step number within the exercise. Omit to use the current step or next step. Examples: 1, 3.
- `type` ("problem" | "solution", optional) - Step type. Omit to keep the current type or default to the problem step. Examples: problem, solution.

Returns: { playground: { exerciseNumber, stepNumber, type, appName, fullPath } }

Examples:
- "Continue to the next incomplete step" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react" }
- "Open exercise 2 step 3 solution" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react", "exerciseNumber": 2, "stepNumber": 3, "type": "solution" }

Next steps:
- Call `open_exercise_step_files` to open the relevant files.
- Use `get_exercise_step_progress_diff` to review remaining changes.

workshopDirectory.description: Absolute or relative path to the workshop root directory. Relative paths are resolved from the current working directory. Passing a /playground path is allowed and will be normalized to the workshop root.

exerciseNumber.description: Exercise number to open (1-based). Omit to use the next incomplete step.

stepNumber.description: Step number to open within the exercise (1-based). Omit to keep the current step or advance.

type.description: Step type to open ("problem" or "solution"). Omit to keep the current type or default to problem.

tools.name: list_saved_playgrounds
tools.description:
List saved playground copies when playground persistence is enabled.

Inputs:
- `workshopDirectory` (string, required) - Absolute path to the workshop root. Examples: /Users/alice/workshops/react-fundamentals.

Returns: { savedPlaygrounds: [{ id, appName, displayName, createdAt, createdAtMs, fullPath }] }

Examples:
- "List saved playgrounds" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react" }

Next steps:
- Call `set_saved_playground` with a savedPlaygroundId to restore a copy.

workshopDirectory.description: Absolute or relative path to the workshop root directory. Relative paths are resolved from the current working directory. Passing a /playground path is allowed and will be normalized to the workshop root.

tools.name: set_saved_playground
tools.description:
Restore the playground from a saved copy.

Inputs:
- `workshopDirectory` (string, required) - Absolute path to the workshop root. Examples: /Users/alice/workshops/react-fundamentals.
- `savedPlaygroundId` (string, optional) - Saved playground id (directory name). Omit to restore the most recent saved copy. Examples: 2026.01.18_11.12.00_01.01.problem.
- `latest` (boolean, optional) - Use the most recent saved playground when true. Examples: true.

Returns: { savedPlayground: { id, appName, displayName, createdAt, fullPath } }

Examples:
- "Restore the most recent saved playground" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react" }
- "Restore a specific saved playground" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react", "savedPlaygroundId": "2026.01.18_11.12.00_01.01.problem" }

Next steps:
- Open relevant files with `open_exercise_step_files` or `open_file`.

workshopDirectory.description: Absolute or relative path to the workshop root directory. Relative paths are resolved from the current working directory. Passing a /playground path is allowed and will be normalized to the workshop root.

savedPlaygroundId.description: Saved playground id to restore (directory name).

latest.description: Use the most recent saved playground when true.

tools.name: update_progress
tools.description:
Mark an Epic lesson as complete or incomplete for the current user.

Inputs:
- `workshopDirectory` (string, required) - Absolute path to the workshop root. Examples: /Users/alice/workshops/react-fundamentals.
- `epicLessonSlug` (string, required) - Lesson slug from `get_exercise_context`, `get_workshop_context`, or `get_what_is_next`. Examples: react-basics-01-intro.
- `complete` (boolean, optional) - Whether to mark complete (default: true). Examples: true, false.

Returns: { epicLessonSlug, complete }

Examples:
- "Mark a lesson complete" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react", "epicLessonSlug": "react-basics-01-intro", "complete": true }

Next steps:
- Call `get_what_is_next` to get the next action.
- Use `get_user_progress` to verify updates.

tools.name: get_diff_between_apps
tools.description:
Return a git diff between two exercise apps by ID (problem vs solution).

Inputs:
- `workshopDirectory` (string, required) - Absolute path to the workshop root. Examples: /Users/alice/workshops/react-fundamentals.
- `app1` (string, required) - First app ID, e.g. "02.03.problem" or "02.03.solution". Examples: 02.03.problem.
- `app2` (string, required) - Second app ID, e.g. "02.03.solution" or "02.03.problem". Examples: 02.03.solution.

Returns: { diff }

Examples:
- "Compare problem and solution for step 2.3" -> { "workshopDirectory": "/Users/alice/workshops/react", "app1": "02.03.problem", "app2": "02.03.solution" }

Next steps:
- Use `set_playground` to open the relevant step.
- Use `open_exercise_step_files` to review changed files.

instructions:
Quick start
- Call `get_what_is_next` first to discover the next required action.
- If the user is not logged in, call `login` and wait for the verification flow.
- Use `set_playground` to move to a step, then `open_exercise_step_files` to open relevant files.

Default behavior
- Use `list_saved_playgrounds` and `set_saved_playground` to restore saved copies when persistence is enabled.
- `workshopDirectory` is required (absolute path preferred; relative paths resolve from the process cwd). Do not pass unexpanded shell placeholders like `$1`.
- Passing a `/playground` path is normalized to the workshop root.
- The user's work-in-progress lives in the `playground` directory.
- `get_exercise_context` defaults to the current playground exercise when `exerciseNumber` is omitted.
- `set_playground` uses the next incomplete step when arguments are omitted.

How to chain tools safely
- Use `get_workshop_context` to learn exercise numbers and topics.
- Use `get_exercise_context` or `get_exercise_step_context` for instructions and IDs.
- Use `update_progress` with `epicLessonSlug` from context tools.
- Re-run `get_what_is_next` after progress updates or when unsure.

Common patterns & examples
- "Help me continue" -> `get_what_is_next` -> follow steps -> `update_progress` -> `get_what_is_next`.
- "Show step 2.3 solution" -> `set_playground` { exerciseNumber: 2, stepNumber: 3, type: "solution" } -> `open_exercise_step_files`.
- "Diff between 02.03 problem and solution" -> `get_diff_between_apps` { app1: "02.03.problem", app2: "02.03.solution" }.
